text: This staff report is about a matter for which Community Council has delegated authority to make a final decision, provided that it is not amended so that it varies with City policy or by-laws. Transportation Services staff have reviewed the need for traffic calming on Overbrook Place, between Dufferin Street and Wilmington Avenue, to address residents' concerns with the speed of traffic. Our assessment indicates the criteria as set out in the traffic calming policy has been satisfied. Therefore, speed humps should be installed on the subject section of Overbrook Place, subject to positive results of the traffic calming poll.

North York Community Council directed that: 1. City Clerk's poll eligible householders on Overbrook Place, between Dufferin Street and Wilmington Avenue, to determine whether residents support the installation of traffic calming, in accordance with the City of Toronto Traffic Calming Policy. 2. Subject to favourable results of the poll, the City Solicitor: a. prepare a by-law to alter sections of the roadway on Overbrook Place, between Dufferin Street and Wilmington Avenue, for traffic calming purposes, generally as shown in the speed hump plan that Transportation Services circulates to residents during the polling process; and b. approve the reduction of the speed limit from 50 km/h to 30 km/h on Overbrook Place, between Dufferin Street and Wilmington Avenue, when speed humps are installed.
